title: Idioms and Proverbs
tagline: The sayings elders use, with the pictures behind them.
canDo: You can understand everyday idioms and proverbs, and use a few yourself

grammar.title: Idioms are verbs: conjugate them
grammar.body: naak mein dam karna, aag bagoola hona, nau do gyarah hona: the last word is an ordinary verb, so it changes like one. usne naak mein dam kar diya; woh aag bagoola ho gayi.

grammar.title: Proverbs are frozen
grammar.body: Proverbs don't change: naach na jaane aangan tedha is said exactly like that, whoever it's about. Some keep old grammar (kya hot for kya hota).

grammar.title: jitna… utna, jaisa… waisa
grammar.body: Paired words build comparisons: jitne munh utni baatein (as many mouths, that many stories), jaisa des waisa bhes (as the country, so the dress).

phrases.roman: daal mein kuch kaala hai
phrases.urdu: دال میں کچھ کالا ہے
phrases.en: Something's fishy
phrases.literal: there's something black in the lentils

phrases.roman: ghar ki murgi daal barabar
phrases.urdu: گھر کی مرغی دال برابر
phrases.en: We undervalue what we already have
phrases.literal: the chicken at home is worth the same as lentils

phrases.roman: oont ke munh mein zeera
phrases.urdu: اونٹ کے منہ میں زیرہ
phrases.en: A drop in the ocean
phrases.literal: a cumin seed in a camel's mouth

phrases.roman: bandar kya jaane adrak ka swaad
phrases.urdu: بندر کیا جانے ادرک کا سواد
phrases.en: It's wasted on someone who can't appreciate it
phrases.literal: what does a monkey know of the taste of ginger?
accept: bandar kya jane adrak ka swad
bandar kya jaane adrak ka sawad

phrases.roman: tum to eid ka chaand ho gaye ho
phrases.urdu: تم تو عید کا چاند ہو گئے ہو
phrases.en: We never see you any more
phrases.literal: you've become the Eid moon
accept: tum to eid ka chand ho gaye ho
tum toh eid ka chaand ho gaye ho
phrases.hook: The Eid moon is seen once a year, briefly, and everyone argues about whether they really saw it.

phrases.roman: woh Nani ki aankhon ka tara hai
phrases.urdu: وہ نانی کی آنکھوں کا تارا ہے
phrases.en: He's the apple of Nani's eye
phrases.literal: he's the star of Nani's eyes
accept: woh nani ki aankhon ka taara hai
wo nani ki ankhon ka tara hai

phrases.roman: bachon ne naak mein dam kar diya hai
phrases.urdu: بچوں نے ناک میں دم کر دیا ہے
phrases.en: The kids have driven me up the wall
phrases.literal: the kids have put my breath in my nose
accept: bachchon ne naak mein dam kar diya hai
bachon ne nak mein dam kar diya hai

phrases.roman: dil baagh baagh ho gaya
phrases.urdu: دل باغ باغ ہو گیا
phrases.en: I'm absolutely delighted
phrases.literal: my heart became a garden, a garden

phrases.roman: Abbu aag bagoola ho gaye
phrases.urdu: ابو آگ بگولا ہو گئے
phrases.en: Abbu was furious
phrases.literal: Abbu became a whirlwind of fire

phrases.roman: chor nau do gyarah ho gaya
phrases.urdu: چور نو دو گیارہ ہو گیا
phrases.en: The thief made a run for it
phrases.literal: the thief became nine-two-eleven
accept: chor nau do gyara ho gaya
chor no do gyarah ho gaya
phrases.hook: 9 + 2 = 11. One moment he was there; then he was arithmetic.

phrases.roman: haath par haath dhare mat baitho
phrases.urdu: ہاتھ پر ہاتھ دھرے مت بیٹھو
phrases.en: Don't just sit there doing nothing
phrases.literal: don't sit with hand placed on hand
accept: haath pe haath dhare mat baitho
hath par hath dhare mat baitho

phrases.roman: naach na jaane aangan tedha
phrases.urdu: ناچ نہ جانے آنگن ٹیڑھا
phrases.en: A bad workman blames his tools
phrases.literal: can't dance, says the courtyard is crooked

phrases.roman: door ke dhol suhane
phrases.urdu: دور کے ڈھول سہانے
phrases.en: The grass is greener on the other side
phrases.literal: distant drums sound sweet

phrases.roman: jaisa des waisa bhes
phrases.urdu: جیسا دیس ویسا بھیس
phrases.en: When in Rome, do as the Romans do
phrases.literal: as the country, so the dress

phrases.roman: ulta chor kotwal ko daante
phrases.urdu: الٹا چور کوتوال کو ڈانٹے
phrases.en: The guilty one is doing the accusing
phrases.literal: backwards: the thief scolds the police chief

phrases.roman: aasman se gira, khajoor mein atka
phrases.urdu: آسمان سے گرا، کھجور میں اٹکا
phrases.en: Out of the frying pan, into the fire
phrases.literal: fell from the sky, got stuck in a date palm
accept: aasman se gira khajoor mein atka
asman se gira khajur mein atka

phrases.roman: ek teer se do shikar
phrases.urdu: ایک تیر سے دو شکار
phrases.en: Two birds with one stone
phrases.literal: two prey with one arrow

phrases.roman: jitne munh utni baatein
phrases.urdu: جتنے منہ اتنی باتیں
phrases.en: Everyone has their own version
phrases.literal: as many mouths, that many stories

phrases.roman: chiragh tale andhera
phrases.urdu: چراغ تلے اندھیرا
phrases.en: The problem is right under your nose
phrases.literal: darkness under the lamp

phrases.roman: qatra qatra darya banta hai
phrases.urdu: قطرہ قطرہ دریا بنتا ہے
phrases.en: Little by little it adds up
phrases.literal: drop by drop a river is made
phrases.note: Also true of learning a language.

phrases.roman: ab pachhtaye kya hot, jab chiriyan chug gayin khet
phrases.urdu: اب پچھتائے کیا ہوت، جب چڑیاں چگ گئیں کھیت
phrases.en: No use crying over spilt milk
phrases.literal: what use is regret now, when the birds have eaten the field
accept: ab pachtaye kya hot jab chidiya chug gayi khet
ab pachhtaye kya hot jab chiriyan chug gayin khet
ab pachtaye kya hot jab chiriya chug gayi khet

phrases.roman: Bilal ne kaha woh library mein hai. Lekin peeche music baj raha tha
phrases.urdu: بلال نے کہا وہ لائبریری میں ہے۔ لیکن پیچھے میوزک بج رہا تھا
phrases.en: Bilal said he's at the library. But there was music playing behind him
phrases.speaker: khala

phrases.roman: Hmm. Daal mein kuch kaala hai
phrases.urdu: ہمم۔ دال میں کچھ کالا ہے
phrases.en: Hmm. Something's fishy
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Yeh bat kharab hai. Is liye out ho gaya
phrases.urdu: یہ بیٹ خراب ہے۔ اس لیے آؤٹ ہو گیا
phrases.en: This bat's no good. That's why I got out
phrases.speaker: bilal

phrases.roman: Naach na jaane, aangan tedha
phrases.urdu: ناچ نہ جانے، آنگن ٹیڑھا
phrases.en: Can't dance, blames the courtyard
phrases.speaker: abbu

phrases.roman: Chashma dhoondh rahi hoon. Kahin nahin mil raha
phrases.urdu: چشمہ ڈھونڈ رہی ہوں۔ کہیں نہیں مل رہا
phrases.en: I'm looking for my glasses. Can't find them anywhere
phrases.speaker: ammi

phrases.roman: Tumhare sar par hai. Chiragh tale andhera
phrases.urdu: تمہارے سر پر ہے۔ چراغ تلے اندھیرا
phrases.en: They're on your head. Darkness under the lamp
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Aao, aao! Tum to eid ka chaand ho gaye ho
phrases.urdu: آؤ، آؤ! تم تو عید کا چاند ہو گئے ہو
phrases.en: Come, come! You've become the Eid moon
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Nani, aap to meri aankhon ka tara hain
phrases.urdu: نانی، آپ تو میری آنکھوں کا تارا ہیں
phrases.en: Nani, you're the apple of my eye
accept: nani aap to meri aankhon ka tara hain
aap to meri aankhon ka tara hain

phrases.roman: Kaam ne naak mein dam kar diya hai, Nani
phrases.urdu: کام نے ناک میں دم کر دیا ہے، نانی
phrases.en: Work has been driving me up the wall, Nani
accept: kaam ne naak mein dam kar diya hai

phrases.roman: Bilal kehta hai London bohat achha hai. Door ke dhol suhane!
phrases.urdu: بلال کہتا ہے لندن بہت اچھا ہے۔ دور کے ڈھول سہانے!
phrases.en: Bilal says London is wonderful. Distant drums sound sweet!
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Sach hai, Nani. Ghar ki murgi daal barabar
phrases.urdu: سچ ہے، نانی۔ گھر کی مرغی دال برابر
phrases.en: True, Nani. We never value what's at home
accept: sach hai nani ghar ki murgi daal barabar

phrases.roman: Wahan bhi theek hai. Jaisa des waisa bhes
phrases.urdu: وہاں بھی ٹھیک ہے۔ جیسا دیس ویسا بھیس
phrases.en: It's fine there too. When in Rome
accept: wahan bhi theek hai jaisa des waisa bhes

phrases.roman: Achha, yeh lo pachaas rupay. Mithai kha lena
phrases.urdu: اچھا، یہ لو پچاس روپے۔ مٹھائی کھا لینا
phrases.en: Right, here's fifty rupees. Buy yourself some sweets
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Shukriya Nani! Dil baagh baagh ho gaya
phrases.urdu: شکریہ نانی! دل باغ باغ ہو گیا
phrases.en: Thank you Nani! I'm delighted
accept: shukriya nani dil baagh baagh ho gaya

phrases.roman: Nani, yeh to oont ke munh mein zeera hai!
phrases.urdu: نانی، یہ تو اونٹ کے منہ میں زیرہ ہے!
phrases.en: Nani, that's a cumin seed in a camel's mouth!
accept: nani yeh to oont ke munh mein zeera hai
yeh to oont ke munh mein zeera hai

phrases.roman: Jeete raho. Qatra qatra darya banta hai
phrases.urdu: جیتے رہو۔ قطرہ قطرہ دریا بنتا ہے
phrases.en: Bless you. Drop by drop, a river is made
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Hahaha! Bandar kya jaane adrak ka swaad
phrases.urdu: ہاہاہا! بندر کیا جانے ادرک کا سواد
phrases.en: Hahaha! What does a monkey know of ginger
phrases.speaker: nani

phrases.roman: Bohat dinon baad main Khala ke ghar gaya.
phrases.urdu: بہت دنوں بعد میں خالہ کے گھر گیا۔
phrases.en: After a long time, I went to Khala's house.

phrases.roman: Arre! Tum to eid ka chaand ho gaye ho!
phrases.urdu: ارے! تم تو عید کا چاند ہو گئے ہو!
phrases.en: Well! You've become the Eid moon!
phrases.speaker: khala

phrases.roman: Maine kaha: Khala, kaam ne naak mein dam kar diya hai.
phrases.urdu: میں نے کہا: خالہ، کام نے ناک میں دم کر دیا ہے۔
phrases.en: I said: Khala, work has been driving me up the wall.

phrases.roman: Kaam? Bilal bhi kaam karta hai, phir bhi har hafte aata hai.
phrases.urdu: کام؟ بلال بھی کام کرتا ہے، پھر بھی ہر ہفتے آتا ہے۔
phrases.en: Work? Bilal works too, and he still comes every week.
phrases.speaker: khala

phrases.roman: Mujhe laga daal mein kuch kaala hai.
phrases.urdu: مجھے لگا دال میں کچھ کالا ہے۔
phrases.en: I felt something was fishy.

phrases.roman: Woh khana khane aata hai. Aur kapde dhulwane. Ek teer se do shikar.
phrases.urdu: وہ کھانا کھانے آتا ہے۔ اور کپڑے دھلوانے۔ ایک تیر سے دو شکار۔
phrases.en: He comes to eat. And to get his washing done. Two birds with one stone.
phrases.speaker: khala

lessons.title: Lentils and camels
lessons.blurb: Half of Urdu's idioms are about food. Nobody is surprised.
lessons.canDo: You can understand and use four everyday food idioms

teach.title: Don't translate. Picture it
teach.info: An idiom means its picture, not its words. Each one here comes with the literal image: learn the image and the meaning sticks.

teach.tip: Chicken is a treat. But the one in your own yard? Might as well be lentils.
For any amount that is nowhere near enough.
For when your effort is not appreciated. Use carefully: you are calling someone a monkey.

exercises.question: What does Nani think?

options.feedback: There are no actual lentils.
It does not. That's her point.

exercises.setup: Khala has just got off the phone.

exercises.prompt: Your salary went up by 1%. Rent went up by 30%. The raise is…

options.feedback: That's about not valuing what you have.
Suspicious, yes. But the idiom you want is about 'not nearly enough'.

exercises.prompt: You cook for six hours. Bilal says “it's fine” without looking up from his phone.

options.feedback: That's 'far too little'.
Nothing fishy. He's just a monkey with ginger.

exercises.explain: Lentils are supposed to be yellow (peela). It's the black (kaala) bit that's suspicious.

lessons.title: Eid moons and whirlwinds
lessons.blurb: Idioms for people: the ones you love, and the ones driving you mad.
lessons.canDo: You can describe people and feelings with idioms

teach.tip: The standard greeting for any relative who hasn't visited in a month.

exercises.prompt: You haven't called Khala in six weeks. Her first words:

options.feedback: She will be delighted. But first, the guilt.
That's what you'd like to do right now.

lessons.title: Nani's proverbs
lessons.blurb: She has one for every situation. Now you'll know which.
lessons.canDo: You can recognise common proverbs and what they're really saying

exercises.question: What is Abbu saying about Bilal?

options.text: He's blaming the bat for his own bad batting

options.feedback: Nobody is dancing. It's a proverb.
The pitch is fine. So is the bat.

exercises.setup: Garden cricket. Bilal has just been bowled. By Nani.

options.feedback: That's the proverb, not the location.
Found. Nani finds everything.

exercises.prompt: You go to the bank and also pick up the dry cleaning next door.

options.feedback: That's about everyone having a different story.
That's 'the grass is greener'.

exercises.prompt: Five relatives, five different versions of what happened at the wedding.

options.feedback: That's 'two birds, one stone'.
That's when the guilty one does the accusing.

exercises.prompt: Type the proverb: “distant drums sound sweet”

lessons.title: Too late, and little by little
lessons.blurb: Three longer ones worth knowing by heart.
lessons.canDo: You can follow longer proverbs when elders use them

teach.tip: Old-fashioned wording ('hot' for 'hota'). Proverbs keep their antique grammar.

exercises.prompt: You escaped a boring wedding conversation and walked straight into Mrs. Butt.

options.feedback: That's 'little by little'.
Close in spirit, but that one is about regret after the fact.

exercises.prompt: The exam was yesterday. Bilal's cousin starts studying today.

options.feedback: Too late for little by little.
That's out of one problem, into another.

exercises.explain: Drops make a river (darya), not a desert (sahra).

exercises.prompt: Type: “drop by drop a river is made”

boss.title: Nani Speaks in Proverbs
boss.blurb: Nani hasn't seen you in a month. She will express this entirely in idioms.
boss.scene: You finally visit Nani. She's on the takht with her paan-daan, and she has been saving these up.
boss.canDo: You can keep up with an elder who talks in idioms, and answer in kind

b.prompt: You've been told off, lovingly. Respond.

options.reaction: Flattery, in idiom. She is defenceless.

d.prompt: Answer a proverb with a proverb.

options.reaction: Fifty rupees last bought a box of mithai in about 1994.

end.title: Proverb for proverb
end.text: You understood every idiom Nani threw at you and threw a few back. She'll tell everyone your Urdu is 'bilkul hamari tarah', just like ours. There is no higher grade.

story.title: The Eid moon
story.blurb: A visit to Khala, conducted entirely in idioms.

questions.question: What does Khala mean by “eid ka chaand”?

options.feedback: The Eid moon is seen rarely. She's telling you off.
It's an idiom: you're as rare as the Eid moon.

questions.question: Why does Bilal visit every week?

options.feedback: Khala knows better: two birds, one arrow.
Khala's version: khana and kapde.
